tldr: A Datadog engineer detailed pairing Claude and Cursor on a real production storage migration on Jul 10, and by Jul 14 MarkTechPost had scored four coding agents — including Claude Code and Cursor — on the same scaffold-to-PR task, turning vendor claims into a head-to-head comparison.
whats_new: Anthropic's own Jul 17 post describes Cursor validating Claude Fable 5 against an internal 'CursorBench' suite covering its hardest 1% of coding tasks before shipping it in production.
why_it_matters: Coding-agent evaluation keeps maturing from vendor claims toward comparable evidence, but a vendor-published case study still isn't independent verification — weigh Cursor's account accordingly until its benchmark methodology is public.

status.detail: Coverage now spans independent cross-agent benchmarking plus a vendor-published case study, with no independent evaluation of Cursor's internal CursorBench criteria yet.

beats.headline: Datadog engineer details pairing Claude and Cursor for a production storage migration
beats.summary: A test-driven migration account shares what worked and what didn't running the two agents together against a real production system.

beats.headline: MarkTechPost scores Mistral Vibe for Code, Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex on one scaffold-to-PR task
beats.summary: Four agents run the same task on the same scaffold, producing a directly comparable score instead of separate vendor claims.

beats.headline: Anthropic publishes Cursor's account of vetting Fable 5 via an internal 'CursorBench'
beats.summary: Cursor describes running Fable 5 against its hardest 1% of coding tasks before shipping it in production — a vendor case study, not independent verification.

open_questions: Does the MarkTechPost scaffold-to-PR scoring hold up under independent replication with different tasks?
Is Cursor's internal 'CursorBench' suite or its results published anywhere reviewable, or is this only Anthropic's characterization?
Will other coding-agent vendors publish comparable internal benchmark methodology, or does Cursor's account stay an outlier?
take_for_builders: Run the same scaffold-to-PR task across your own agent shortlist rather than trusting vendor claims, and treat a vendor-published case study like Cursor's CursorBench account as anecdotal until its methodology is public.
